newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks trade flat with weaker bias.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks trade flat with weaker bias.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 19514.75 +239.42 LME CASH NICKEL US$7240 +10.0
CANDLR 1.3810 LME CASH ALUM US$1587.0 -23.0
CAN 30-YR 110.90 -0.20 BRENT CRUDE US$17.97 -0.32
* Toronto stocks traded steady but held a weaker bias as losers outnumbered winners 231 to 184. * Golds higher despite Bre-X fraud. * 8.2 million shares traded worth C$169.7 million.
Toronto stocks quietly traded flat at Monday's open, held steady by a buoyant gold group despite a bias to the weaker side.

"We should do okay today," one trader said as the key gold sector rose more than one percent after news that Bre-X Minerals Ltd and its Busang site, once touted as the world's largest gold discovery, was a fraud.

Consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd said in a report that it found evidence of large-scale tampering with core samples taken from Busang. "Whatever was supposed to be found in Indonesia isn't there anymore," he said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange stopped Bre-X trading, and has not said when it will re-open.
"I think it's a pretty nonchalant day," another trader said. "There's fall-out from Bre-X and other areas. But the volume isn't there."
Some junior gold issues sold off as investors debated the validity of small mining companies. "Until this came up, Canada was the mining capital for the world," the first trader said.
Losers edged out winners 231 to 184 in early trading while 197 remained flat.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indices rose, led by golds, consumer products and transportation. Media and banks lost ground.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Shares in small gold miners, especially those with Indonesian projects, dropped. Scorpion Minerals Inc plunged 1.20 to 1.70 while Indochina Goldfields Ltd dipped 1.00 to 12.00.
* Barrick Gold jumped 0.55 to 31.95, topping most actives as bullion prices ticked upward.
* Banks relinquished some of their recent gains. Bank of Montreal lost 0.80 to 69.25 in brisk trading.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
